identity.title: Complete genome analysis, safety assessment and probiotic potential of Limosilactobacillus oris BSLO1801.

content.abstract: Clarifying the genomic information of probiotic strains is an important prerequisite for their application. Limosilactobacillus oris BSLO1801 (BSLO1801), a strain derived from the manure of high-yield laying hens, has shown promise in enhancing the performance of poultry and is considered for use as a feed additive. This research assessed the safety profile and probiotic attributes of BSLO1801 through a combination of in vitro and in vivo experiments, complemented by whole-genome sequencing analysis. The genomic evaluation revealed that BSLO1801 comprises a single chromosome and five plasmids, and it lacks CRISPR sequences, classical virulence factors, and oriT transfer sites. Among the 17 antibiotic resistance genes identified, only plasmid-borne tet (M) was classified as an acquired resistance gene, while the other 16 were intrinsic chromosomal resistance genes. The genome was thoroughly annotated with databases such as COG, GO, KEGG, CAZy, identifying a wealth of genes associated with probiotic functionalities, particularly those involved in carbohydrate metabolism. In vitro assays showed BSLO1801 had good gastrointestinal tolerance and moderate EPS/DPPH antioxidant activity; its adhesion measured on human Caco-2 cells cannot directly represent avian intestinal performance, and no haemolysis was observed., while exhibiting no haemolytic properties. No significant changes in body weight or organ indices were observed in mice following oral administration of BSLO1801. In conclusion, no adverse effects were observed for BSLO1801 under all tested conditions; this strain possesses favorable in vitro probiotic properties and comprehensively annotated genomic features, making it a promising candidate for subsequent validation as a poultry feed-additive probiotic.
